project.name: ai201-project5-mixtape-starter
project.description: A social music app where friends share songs, build collaborative playlists, and track listening stats. This is the starter repo for Project 5: Mixtape Bug Hunt, with five open issues to find, fix, and document in the services layer.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Flask application factory that configures the database, registers all route blueprints, and creates tables on startup for the Mixtape social music app.

nodes.name: create_app
nodes.summary: Builds and configures the Flask app instance, wiring up the database connection, initializing SQLAlchemy, registering the users/songs/playlists/notifications blueprints, and creating all tables.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the SQLAlchemy ORM data model for the Mixtape app, including Users, Songs, Tags, ListeningEvents, Ratings, Playlists, and Notifications along with their relationships and serialization helpers.

nodes.name: generate_uuid
nodes.summary: Generates a random UUID string used as the default primary key value for model records.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: ORM model representing an app user, tracking profile info, listening streak state (listening_streak, last_listened_at), friendships, playlists, and notifications, with a to_dict serializer.

nodes.name: Tag
nodes.summary: ORM model representing a genre/mood tag that can be attached to songs for search and categorization.

nodes.name: Song
nodes.summary: ORM model representing a song entry with metadata, tags, and shared-by attribution, with a to_dict serializer for API responses.

nodes.name: ListeningEvent
nodes.summary: ORM model recording a single instance of a user listening to a song, used to compute activity feeds and listening streaks.

nodes.name: Rating
nodes.summary: ORM model storing a user's rating of a song, used for recommendations and feed activity.

nodes.name: Playlist
nodes.summary: ORM model representing a collaborative playlist, its creator, collaboration flag, and ordered song entries via the playlist_entries association table.

nodes.name: Notification
nodes.summary: ORM model representing a user notification (e.g. song added, rating received) with a read/unread flag and to_dict serializer.

nodes.name: seed_data.py
nodes.summary: Standalone script that resets the database and seeds it with sample users, friendships, tags, songs, listening events, playlists, and notifications for local development and manual testing.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: Drops and recreates all tables, then inserts a full set of demo data (users, friendships, tags, songs, listening events, playlists, and notifications) to populate a working local dataset.

nodes.name: playlist_service.py
nodes.summary: Service layer handling playlist creation and retrieval, including fetching a playlist's ordered songs and a user's owned playlists.
nodes.languageNotes: get_playlist_songs slices the query result with songs[:-1] before returning, which drops the last song even though the docstring says it returns all songs in playlist order — a likely off-by-one bug worth investigating as part of the project's bug hunt.

nodes.name: create_playlist
nodes.summary: Validates that the creating user exists, then creates and persists a new Playlist row with the given name and collaboration flag.

nodes.name: get_playlist_songs
nodes.summary: Fetches all songs in a playlist ordered by their position via the playlist_entries join table, but truncates the last item from the returned list (songs[:-1]) before serializing.

nodes.name: get_playlist
nodes.summary: Retrieves a playlist's metadata (without its songs) as a dict, raising if the playlist does not exist.

nodes.name: get_user_playlists
nodes.summary: Returns all playlists created by a given user as a list of serialized dicts.

nodes.name: streak_service.py
nodes.summary: Service layer implementing listening-streak logic: recording listening events and updating/reading a user's consecutive-day listening streak.
nodes.languageNotes: update_listening_streak special-cases today.weekday() != 6 (Sunday) when deciding whether to increment the streak, so a consecutive-day listen falling on a Sunday resets the streak to 1 instead of incrementing — likely one of the project's intentional bugs, and directly exercised by test_streak_increments_on_sunday.

nodes.name: record_listening_event
nodes.summary: Validates the user exists, creates a ListeningEvent for the given song, and triggers a streak update before committing the transaction.

nodes.name: update_listening_streak
nodes.summary: Computes the day delta since the user's last listen and updates listening_streak: starts at 1 for first-ever listens, no-ops for same-day repeats, increments for consecutive days (except when today is Sunday, where it resets), and resets to 1 otherwise.

nodes.name: get_streak
nodes.summary: Looks up a user by ID and returns their current listening_streak value, raising if the user is not found.

nodes.name: test_playlists.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for the playlist service, covering full-song retrieval, ordering, and behavior on empty playlists using an in-memory test app and seeded fixtures.

nodes.name: app
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that creates a fresh Flask app with tables created for the test, and drops them afterward for isolation.

nodes.name: seed_playlist
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that seeds a user, songs, and a playlist with ordered playlist_entries rows to be used by playlist retrieval tests.

nodes.name: test_playlist_returns_all_songs
nodes.summary: Asserts that get_playlist_songs returns every song that was added to a seeded playlist.

nodes.name: test_playlist_returns_songs_in_order
nodes.summary: Asserts that get_playlist_songs returns songs in the order they were added to the playlist.

nodes.name: test_empty_playlist_returns_empty_list
nodes.summary: Asserts that get_playlist_songs returns an empty list for a playlist with no songs added.

nodes.name: test_streaks.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for the streak service, covering initial streak creation, consecutive-day increments, same-day no-ops, streak resets after a skipped day, and behavior when a consecutive listen falls on a Sunday.

nodes.name: app
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that creates a fresh Flask app with tables created for the test, and drops them afterward for isolation.

nodes.name: user
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that creates and commits a single test User to be used across streak tests.

nodes.name: test_streak_starts_at_1_for_new_user
nodes.summary: Asserts that update_listening_streak sets listening_streak to 1 for a user with no prior listens.

nodes.name: test_streak_increments_on_consecutive_day
nodes.summary: Asserts that listening on two consecutive calendar days increments the streak from 1 to 2.

nodes.name: test_streak_does_not_double_count_same_day
nodes.summary: Asserts that listening twice on the same calendar day does not increment the streak further.

nodes.name: test_streak_resets_after_skipped_day
nodes.summary: Asserts that skipping a day between listens resets the streak back to 1.

nodes.name: test_streak_increments_on_sunday
nodes.summary: Asserts that a consecutive-day listen falling on a Sunday still increments the streak, directly targeting the weekday-based special case in update_listening_streak.

nodes.name: playlists.py
nodes.summary: Flask blueprint exposing playlist HTTP routes: create a playlist, fetch playlist details, list a playlist's songs, and add a song to a playlist, delegating business logic to the playlist and notification services.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Handles POST / to create a new playlist from JSON body fields (name, created_by, is_collaborative), validating required fields and delegating to create_playlist.

nodes.name: get_detail
nodes.summary: Handles GET /<playlist_id> to return playlist details, returning 404 when the playlist is not found.

nodes.name: get_songs
nodes.summary: Handles GET /<playlist_id>/songs to list the songs in a playlist along with a count.

nodes.name: add_song
nodes.summary: Handles POST /<playlist_id>/songs to add a song to a playlist by delegating to the notification service's add_to_playlist, which also triggers a notification.

nodes.name: users.py
nodes.summary: Flask blueprint exposing user-related HTTP routes: fetch a user, get listening streak, list notifications, and mark a notification as read.

nodes.name: get_user
nodes.summary: Handles GET /<user_id> to fetch a user by ID and return its dict representation, or a 404 if not found.

nodes.name: streak
nodes.summary: Handles GET /<user_id>/streak to return a user's current listening streak via the streak service.

nodes.name: notifications
nodes.summary: Handles GET /<user_id>/notifications, parsing the unread_only query flag and returning the user's notifications with a count.

nodes.name: read_notification
nodes.summary: Handles POST /notifications/<notification_id>/read to mark a notification as read via the notification service.

nodes.name: notification_service.py
nodes.summary: Service layer handling notification creation/retrieval, adding songs to playlists (which triggers notifications to the original sharer), and saving song ratings.
nodes.languageNotes: add_to_playlist and rate_song use local imports (Playlist model, playlist_service) to avoid circular import issues between services.

nodes.name: create_notification
nodes.summary: Creates and persists a Notification record for a given user with a type and body message.

nodes.name: add_to_playlist
nodes.summary: Validates a song, adding user, and playlist exist, appends the song to the playlist if not already present, and notifies the song's original sharer unless they are the one adding it.

nodes.name: rate_song
nodes.summary: Validates a rating score (1-5), song, and user, then creates or updates the user's Rating for that song.

nodes.name: get_notifications
nodes.summary: Queries notifications for a user, optionally filtered to unread only, ordered by most recent first, and serializes them to dicts.

nodes.name: mark_as_read
nodes.summary: Marks a notification's read flag as true and commits the change, raising an error if the notification does not exist.

nodes.name: songs.py
nodes.summary: Flask blueprint defining the song-related HTTP routes: search, song detail, rating, and listen-tracking endpoints that delegate to the search, notification, and streak services.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Route handler for GET /search that validates the query parameter and returns matching songs via search_songs, wrapped with a result count.

nodes.name: get_song_detail
nodes.summary: Route handler for GET /<song_id> that fetches a single song's details and returns a 404 JSON error when the song is not found.

nodes.name: rate
nodes.summary: Route handler for POST /<song_id>/rate that validates the request body and submits a rating via the notification service, returning the created rating or a validation error.

nodes.name: listen
nodes.summary: Route handler for POST /<song_id>/listen that records a listening event for a user via the streak service and returns the created event or a validation error.

nodes.name: search_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements song search and single-song lookup logic, querying the Song model by title/artist and joining tag associations; the outerjoin without a distinct() call can produce duplicate results for multi-tag songs.
nodes.languageNotes: search_songs performs an outerjoin against the song_tags association table but does not deduplicate the resulting rows, so a song with multiple tags can appear multiple times in the results — a likely source of the bug this project's test suite targets.

nodes.name: search_songs
nodes.summary: Searches songs by case-insensitive title or artist match, joining the song_tags table to include tag associations; missing distinct() causes duplicate rows for songs with several tags.

nodes.name: get_song
nodes.summary: Fetches a single song by its UUID, raising ValueError when no matching song exists.

nodes.name: test_search.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for the search service covering matching-song search and, notably, duplicate-prevention behavior for songs with zero, one, or multiple tags.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes dedicated fixtures (app, seed_songs) that seed users, tags, songs, and song_tags associations, and several tests asserting no duplicate rows are returned regardless of tag count — directly exercising the search_songs join/duplicate bug.

nodes.name: app
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that creates a Flask app instance with an in-memory database, creating and tearing down all tables around each test.

nodes.name: seed_songs
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that seeds a test user, several tags, songs, and song-tag associations used across the search tests.

nodes.name: test_search_returns_matching_songs
nodes.summary: Verifies that search_songs returns songs matching the query string.

nodes.name: test_search_no_duplicates_single_tag_song
nodes.summary: Asserts that a song with exactly one tag appears only once in the search results.

nodes.name: test_search_no_duplicates_multi_tag_song
nodes.summary: Asserts that a song with multiple tags appears only once in the search results, guarding against duplicate rows from the outerjoin in search_songs.

nodes.name: test_search_no_duplicates_no_tag_song
nodes.summary: Asserts that a song with no tags still appears exactly once in the search results.

nodes.name: test_search_returns_empty_for_no_match
nodes.summary: Verifies that search_songs returns an empty list when no songs match the query.

nodes.name: feed.py
nodes.summary: Flask Blueprint exposing the friends-listening-now and activity-feed HTTP endpoints, delegating business logic to services/feed_service.py and translating ValueError into 404 JSON responses.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker file that makes services/ importable as a Python package.

nodes.name: feed_service.py
nodes.summary: Service layer implementing the Friends Listening Now and general activity feed logic, querying ListeningEvent rows for a user's friends and shaping the results into dicts for the API. This is the file that contains the open 'shows people from yesterday' bug referenced in the README.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLAlchemy ORM query chaining with a fixed 24-hour RECENT_THRESHOLD cutoff for the 'listening now' feed, distinct from the unfiltered, limit-based activity feed.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker file that makes tests/ importable as a Python package for pytest discovery.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore-pattern configuration for the Understand-Anything analysis tool, excluding paths that should not be scanned when building the project's knowledge graph.

nodes.name: listening_now
nodes.summary: Route handler for GET /<user_id>/listening-now that calls get_friends_listening_now and returns the feed as JSON, or a 404 error if the user is not found.

nodes.name: activity
nodes.summary: Route handler for GET /<user_id>/activity that calls get_activity_feed and returns the feed as JSON, or a 404 error if the user is not found.

nodes.name: get_friends_listening_now
nodes.summary: Queries ListeningEvent rows for the user's friends within a 24-hour RECENT_THRESHOLD window, deduplicates to the most recent song per friend, and returns friend/song/listened_at dicts ordered by recency.

nodes.name: get_activity_feed
nodes.summary: Returns the most recent N listening events across all of a user's friends, unfiltered by recency, as friend/song/listened_at dicts ordered by most recent first.

tour.title: Project Overview & Bug Hunt
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Mixtape is: a social music app where friends share songs, build collaborative playlists, and track listening stats. The README lists the five open bugs you're hunting, all of which live in the services/ layer, and explicitly instructs you to trace each bug from its HTTP route down through its service rather than jumping straight to the fix.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: app.py is the Flask application factory: it configures the database connection, registers every route blueprint (playlists, users, songs, feed), and creates the database tables on startup. With a fan-in of 9, nearly every service and test module in the codebase imports this file to get its db handle, making it the load-bearing hub you must understand before anything else.
tour.languageLesson: Flask's application factory pattern centralizes app configuration and blueprint registration in one place, keeping route modules decoupled from app setup and making the app easier to test in isolation.

tour.title: The Data Model
tour.description: models.py defines the SQLAlchemy ORM classes that every other module depends on: Users, Songs, Tags, ListeningEvents, Ratings, Playlists, and Notifications. It has the highest fan-in in the entire project (10 incoming references), meaning it is the shared vocabulary that routes, services, and tests all speak. As the README advises, understanding these tables first makes every bug you'll investigate next much easier to reason about.

tour.title: Issue #1: Streak Route to Service
tour.description: Follow the README's prescribed reading pattern: routes/users.py exposes the HTTP endpoint that records a listening event, then calls into services/streak_service.py to update the user's consecutive-day streak. This is the first bug hunt stop — a user reports their streak keeps resetting even though they listen every day, and the fix requires tracing this exact call chain rather than guessing from the endpoint alone.
tour.languageLesson: Python's datetime.weekday() returns 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday. A guard clause like `if today.weekday() != 6` silently special-cases Sundays — a classic off-by-one-day trap when reasoning about 'is this consecutive?' logic across week boundaries.

tour.title: Issue #1 Verified: Streak Tests
tour.description: test_streaks.py is the pytest suite for streak_service.py, and it already contains test_streak_increments_on_sunday — a test written specifically to catch the Sunday reset bug from Step 4. This shows the project's workflow: the test layer sits directly above each service and gives you a fast way to confirm whether your fix actually resolves the reported issue before you move on.

tour.title: Issue #2: Friends Feed Route to Service
tour.description: routes/feed.py exposes the 'Friends Listening Now' and activity-feed endpoints, both of which delegate to services/feed_service.py. This service contains the second open bug: the feed shows people from yesterday, which points to a suspect cutoff or RECENT_THRESHOLD calculation used to decide what counts as 'recent'. Note that this is the only route/service pair the README itself links to directly via its own documentation edges, signaling it's a focal point of the exercise.

tour.title: Issue #3: Song Search Route to Service
tour.description: routes/songs.py is the busiest route module in the project (fan-out of 6), fanning out to search, notification, and streak services. Trace its search endpoint down into services/search_service.py, where an outerjoin against the song_tags table is missing a .distinct() call — producing duplicate rows whenever a song has more than one tag. This is the third bug: the same song appearing twice in search results.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy's outerjoin against a many-to-many association table (like song_tags) multiplies each row by the number of matching join partners. Without .distinct(), a song with 3 tags returns 3 identical rows — a common ORM pitfall whenever a query joins across a one-to-many or many-to-many relationship purely to filter or search.

tour.title: Issue #3 Verified: Search Tests
tour.description: test_search.py is the pytest suite covering search_service.py, and it already includes coverage aimed at duplicate-prevention behavior. Reading this test before fixing the bug from Step 7 tells you exactly what output shape the fix needs to produce — a set of unique songs regardless of how many tags they carry.

tour.title: Issue #4: Notifications for Ratings vs Playlists
tour.description: services/notification_service.py handles three responsibilities: creating and retrieving notifications, adding songs to playlists, and saving song ratings. Both routes/songs.py (for rating) and routes/playlists.py (for adding songs) call into it, but only add_to_playlist creates a notification — rate_song does not, even though users expect to be notified either way. This asymmetry between two sibling functions in the same file is the fourth open bug.

tour.title: Issue #5: Playlist Route to Service
tour.description: routes/playlists.py exposes the endpoint for viewing a playlist's songs, which calls services/playlist_service.py's get_playlist_songs function. That function returns songs[:-1] — a Python slice that silently drops the last element of the list — so the final song a friend added to a shared playlist never shows up. This is the fifth and final bug from the README's list, and it demonstrates how an easily-missed slicing mistake can hide in otherwise working code.
tour.languageLesson: Python's negative slice indices count from the end of a sequence: list[:-1] returns every element except the last one. It's a useful idiom for trimming a trailing item on purpose, but an easy off-by-one mistake to introduce accidentally when the intent was list[:] or list[:len(list)].

tour.title: Issue #5 Verified: Playlist Tests
tour.description: test_playlists.py is the pytest suite for playlist_service.py. Running it after fixing the slicing bug from Step 10 confirms that get_playlist_songs now returns every song a friend added, closing out the bug-hunt workflow established across Steps 4 through 11: route leads to service, service leads to test.

tour.title: Seeding & Dependencies
tour.description: seed_data.py is a standalone script that resets and repopulates the database with sample users, songs, and playlists, giving you realistic data to exercise all five bugs against locally. requirements.txt lists the project's dependencies — Flask, Flask-SQLAlchemy, SQLAlchemy, python-dotenv, and pytest — which together explain how the app, the ORM, and the test suite you used in Steps 5, 8, and 11 all fit together.
